title: Dead Hang Fix for Taller Posture
style: Japanese ukiyo-e woodblock print, textured washi paper, clean plain warm background, elegant carved-line shading, consistent portrait 2:3 slide composition
character: Same 19–20-year-old adult character in every slide, athletic but natural build, fully clothed in a simple dark indigo tank top, cream shorts, ankle socks, and training shoes; friendly face, tied-back black hair, no accessories
voice: Upbeat, friendly, brisk delivery with a light echo effect; energetic but clear for word-by-word subtitles.

exercises.name: DEAD HANG
exercises.a: Portrait 2:3 image, Japanese ukiyo-e woodblock print on textured washi paper, same adult character centered with generous margins, top 18% of the image completely empty, whole body visible, no text, no letters, no numbers. Front-facing camera, pull-up bar runs horizontally just below the empty top band. Character hangs from the bar with both hands overhand shoulder-width apart, palms facing away; hands are the only body parts touching the bar, feet are off the floor and not touching anything. WRONG FORM: elbows straight but shoulders shrugged high up toward the ears, neck compressed, head tucked forward, upper back rounded, ribs flared, pelvis loose, legs hanging slightly bent with toes pointed downward. Keep same angle and framing as pose b.
exercises.b: Portrait 2:3 image, Japanese ukiyo-e woodblock print on textured washi paper, same adult character centered with generous margins, top 18% of the image completely empty, whole body visible, no text, no letters, no numbers. Front-facing camera, pull-up bar runs horizontally just below the empty top band. Character hangs from the bar with both hands overhand shoulder-width apart, palms facing away; hands are the only body parts touching the bar, feet are off the floor and not touching anything. RIGHT FORM: elbows straight, shoulders gently pulled down away from the ears, neck long, chin neutral, chest open, ribs stacked, pelvis neutral, legs long and together with toes relaxed downward. Keep same angle and framing as pose a.

exercises.name: SCAP PULL-UPS
exercises.a: Portrait 2:3 image, Japanese ukiyo-e woodblock print on textured washi paper, same adult character centered with generous margins, top 18% of the image completely empty, whole body visible, no text, no letters, no numbers. Front-facing camera, pull-up bar runs horizontally just below the empty top band. START POSITION of a scapular pull-up: character hangs from the bar with both hands overhand shoulder-width apart, palms facing away; hands touch the bar, feet hang freely above the floor and touch nothing. Arms are straight, shoulders are lifted upward under control, body is at the lowest point, chest relaxed, legs straight and together. Same camera angle and framing as pose b.
exercises.b: Portrait 2:3 image, Japanese ukiyo-e woodblock print on textured washi paper, same adult character centered with generous margins, top 18% of the image completely empty, whole body visible, no text, no letters, no numbers. Front-facing camera, pull-up bar runs horizontally just below the empty top band. TOP POSITION of a scapular pull-up: character still hangs with both hands overhand shoulder-width apart, palms facing away; hands touch the bar, feet hang freely above the floor and touch nothing. Arms stay straight, shoulder blades pull down and slightly back, shoulders move far away from ears, chest lifts, torso rises several inches higher than pose a, legs straight and together. Same camera angle and framing as pose a.

result: Portrait 2:3 image, Japanese ukiyo-e woodblock print on textured washi paper, same adult character centered with generous margins, top 18% of the image completely empty, whole body visible, no text, no letters, no numbers. Plain clean warm background. Character stands on the floor facing camera, both feet hip-width apart and fully touching the ground, knees soft, pelvis neutral, ribs stacked, shoulders relaxed down and back, neck long, chin level, tall proud posture, happy confident smile, arms relaxed at sides.

lines.hook: Most dead hangs fail because your shoulders climb to your ears.
lines.ex1: Keep your neck long and pull shoulders gently down.
lines.ex2: Scapular pull-ups teach control and help you stand taller.
lines.takeaway: Two minutes daily: decompress, reset, walk tall.
